title: Intermittent gateway latency
executive_summary: api-gateway P99 latency rose about 18.5% (baseline mean 252.9 ms to 299.6 ms) with onset around 19:40Z and a peak of 557 ms at 19:45Z, consistent with the reported T0 of 19:45Z. The rise is small, p95, error rate, timeout rate, request rate and CPU were flat, and no deployments or config changes occurred in the 18:00-20:10Z window. Over half of the gateway and downstream telemetry is missing after about 19:35-19:50Z, so the cause cannot be confirmed. The most notable signal is a recurring slow statement SELECT report_rollup() on postgres (11.7 s at 19:30Z, 15.8 s at 19:40Z, 14.5 s at 20:03Z). Its timing is suggestive but not proven to affect gateway latency, and postgres's own metrics show no change.

hypotheses.description: Long-running report_rollup() queries on postgres hold resources/connections and slow requests that traverse the gateway's upstream services (order/auth/payment/user), raising gateway P99. Mechanism: Periodic heavy report job executes for 11-16 s; if it contends with OLTP queries or holds locks/connections, requests waiting on DB calls see elevated tail latency, showing up as gateway P99 spikes at 19:40-19:45Z.

root_cause_statement: Root cause could not be conclusively established with the available evidence.
corrective_actions: Pull request-level traces for api-gateway between 19:35Z and 19:50Z to attribute the tail latency to a specific upstream call.
Review the report_rollup() schedule and, if it is confirmed to interfere, move it off the peak path or add a statement timeout.
preventive_actions: Add alerting on gateway P99 with a deviation threshold, so tail regressions are detected even when the average stays flat.
Fix telemetry pipeline gaps so that per-service metrics are complete during incidents.
monitoring_recommendations: Track postgres slow-statement duration for report_rollup() and alert above 5 s.
Track gateway P99 and P99 per upstream dependency, plus gateway connection-pool utilisation.
Monitor telemetry completeness (datapoint availability) per service.
limitations: Tool budget was partly used; the investigation was not exhaustive.

Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: Root cause could not be conclusively established with the available evidence. The evidence does not establish a root cause for the intermittent gateway P99 increase. The rise is modest and confined to the tail (p95 and error rates are flat), with no deployments or config changes. Heavy telemetry gaps weaken all conclusions after about 19:35-19:50Z. The recurring slow report_rollup() statements on postgres are the most promising lead but are not supported by postgres's own latency or connection metrics. Status is INCONCLUSIVE.
